title: Give every goal that reaches Daniel a control he can press
ask:
A goal that escalates to the CEO but declares no route renders, on his own pillar page, as: "not prepped — VP of Engineering (Elena Volkov) owes you a card on this before it is fair to ask". That is HQ naming a problem, putting it at the top of his screen, and then offering him nothing — the exact failure the standing rule against dead ends forbids, and he hit it on 2026-09-19 reading the Engineering page.

Two goals are in that state right now: engineering/build-branch-builds-green (red because the newest CI run on main failed) and, until 2026-09-19, engineering/automatic-release-pipeline (now routed to the Q-111 card). Sweep every goal file for a path_to_green whose route is kind "none" and which can reach him, and give each one a real destination.

The general fix has two halves. First, every escalating goal gets either a route or a path_to_green.action, so routeControl() in hq/static/pillars.js always has a button to draw. Second — the more useful half — a goal whose reading already knows where the evidence is should route there automatically: a failing CI goal knows the run URL it just read, so the control should be "See the failing run", not a confession that nobody wrote a card. Consider making reading.url a fallback route in routeControl rather than something only the attest path uses.

The self-accusing string should not survive the sweep. If a goal genuinely has no next step, that is a defect in the goal, not a sentence to render.
first_action: Read routeControl() and the g-orphan branch in hq/static/pillars.js, then grep hq/data/goals/*.json for '"kind": "none"' and list which of those goals can escalate.
source_message: Daniel asked what the Engineering headline was telling him. The undefined, the bare count and the ambiguous wording were fixed in that session; this is the part of the same block that was left — a finding with no way to act on it.
result:
Done and on main. The sentence is gone from the code, not just from today's data: routeControl() in hq/static/pillars.js no longer has a branch that can render it. The last resort is now a button that files the card the confession said you were owed — to the seat that owns the goal, carrying the goal's own statement, its last reading, and the fact that nobody wrote down the way back. I pressed it on a test goal and read the card it made, then deleted it.

Ahead of that, a goal whose check read a remote address routes there: the failing build's control is now 'See the failing run', both in the headline and on the row, and a reading that carries a URL with no situation attached is taken the same way.

The sweep: every goal that could reach you and declared no route now has one. Build branch builds green had an empty narrative and now says to open the run, fix what it names and push to main. Games deterministically replayable and Rights on record for every asset had a route of kind none and now carry a filing action. Project plans and program report always up to date had nothing measuring it, no narrative and no action, and now says what would measure it and offers to put building that check on the Program Lead's list. The three buttons name the seat rather than a bare first name, and the one on the Finance goal was changed to match.

Verified by reading the pages in the browser, not the code: the Engineering page's headline and both open rows, the parked Art, Product and Finance goals rendered through the real row renderer, and a synthetic goal with nothing on it at all. No page carries a dead end. The unused style for it was deleted too.

follow_ups.title: Measure whether the program report is actually current
follow_ups.first_action: Add a reading for the program-report goal in hq that compares the program report's last-updated time against the newest commit and the newest work item, and writes the result (with a url to the report) into the goal file so the goal can go green or red on its own.
follow_ups.why: The sweep gave that goal a button but it still has nothing measuring it, so it can only ever sit red.

follow_ups.title: Make the build reject a goal that reaches Daniel with no way back
follow_ups.first_action: Add a python check over hq/data/goals/*.json asserting that any goal able to escalate to the CEO has a route of kind other than none, or a path_to_green.action, or a reading.url; wire it into .github/workflows/tests.yml alongside the existing checks, with a --self-test that plants a bad goal and proves it is caught.
follow_ups.why: routeControl() is now safe, but nothing stops the next goal from being added with no destination.

recommend.question: The program-report goal has nothing measuring it — build the measurement, or retire the goal?
recommend.answer: Build the measurement; keep the goal.
recommend.why: It is a commitment the studio actually holds itself to, and an unmeasured goal on your page is the same dead end in a different costume.
recommend.instead: Drop it, if you would rather read the program report yourself than have HQ tell you when it has gone stale.

subject: How HQ works
